channel.title: Webskan – blog
channel.description: Website health for small businesses and the developers who ship for them: speed, security, SEO, accessibility.

item.title: Make your coding agent verify every deploy: a CLAUDE.md block, a CI step and a definition of done
item.description: A CLAUDE.md block, a CI step that fails on high-severity findings, and a definition of done for a live site – with the finding ids behind each line.

item.title: Your deploy just published .env: exposed .git, .env, SQL dumps and backups on live sites – and a 60-second check
item.description: How secrets end up in the web root, what attackers do with them, a 60-second curl check that matches content signatures instead of trusting HTTP 200, and the server fixes.

item.title: Website backup: what you really have, what you don't, and a 15-minute check
item.description: What a website backup must contain, what hosts actually promise, the 3-2-1 rule in plain words and a 15-minute check that tells you whether you can recover after a hack or a broken update.

item.title: How to tell your website has been hacked: nine symptoms, a 10-minute check and what to do first
item.description: Nine symptoms an owner can spot alone, a 10-minute check (including how to see the site the way Google does), first steps in the right order and the Search Console review request.

item.title: Google Business Profile vs your website: what has to match and how to check it in 15 minutes
item.description: Ten places where your Google listing and your business website must say the same thing, a 15-minute test from your phone, and a symptom → cause → who fixes it table.

item.title: Your SSL certificate is expiring: what customers see, how to check the date and how to never repeat it
item.description: What customers see after a certificate expires, eight reasons renewal fails, a 60-second expiry check and a plan so it never happens again.

item.title: Contact form not working? How to check it in 10 minutes
item.description: Eight reasons enquiries vanish, a step-by-step test and a symptom → cause → who fixes it table.

item.title: How to read a PageSpeed Insights report (without a developer)
item.description: What in a PageSpeed report actually matters, what the common messages mean, and how to turn it into a to-do list for your webmaster.

item.title: What a slow website costs you: the numbers to know before you pay for optimisation
item.description: Four studies with real numbers, four ways a slow site loses money, and a five-minute calculation for your own business.

item.title: Audit the website your coding agent just shipped
item.description: Coding agents ship sites fast and skip the outside view. The checks that catch what they miss, and how to give the agent a build, deploy, audit, fix, recheck loop.

item.title: WordPress security: 10 settings you can fix in an hour
item.description: Ten WordPress settings that close the most common ways into a small-business website. No developer needed, one hour of work.

item.title: HTTPS is not enough: 7 things that break behind the padlock
item.description: A padlock in the browser does not mean your site is set up correctly. Seven common certificate and redirect problems, how to spot and fix them.

item.title: Website launch checklist: 24 things to check after your new site goes live
item.description: The things that most often break when a new website launches, and how to check each one in a minute.

item.title: The European Accessibility Act and your website: who must comply, who is exempt, what to do
item.description: Who the EAA covers, the microenterprise exemption, what WCAG 2.1 AA means in practice, the penalties, and a one-week plan.

item.title: Why your website is slow on mobile (and what to do about it)
item.description: The five most common causes of a slow mobile site, how to spot them in PageSpeed and the order to fix them in.

item.title: HTTP security headers in plain English
item.description: The six HTTP headers every scanner flags: what they do, what they protect against and how to enable them without breaking your site.

item.title: Core Web Vitals in plain English: LCP, INP and CLS
item.description: What Core Web Vitals are, which thresholds Google uses and what to fix first.
